correctness.rationale: Each completed greedy arch supplies either bit, and greedily aiming for the successive arch-ending bits followed by a bit missing from the rest constructs an absent subsequence of length one greater. Thus the index is exactly the arch count. A direct enumeration gives a cross-check of the continuation-state proof: for k≥1 the k arch lengths contribute (z²/(1−z))^k, the internal changes t^k, the first orientation 2, the k−1 inter-arch boundaries (1+t)^(k−1), and the empty-or-unary tail 1+z(1+t)/(1−z). This is the stated coefficient of u^k. Its two terms yield exactly the two binomial contributions and r=k,…,2k−1 when n=2k, adding r=2k at n≥2k+1. The n<2k terms vanish, and k=0 has just the empty word or the two positive unary words at each length. An independent program builds all subsequence sets by length and agrees with every joint cell for n=0,…,12, including the zero cells and the support assertions.
residual_risks: The independent finite check through length 12 is corroboration, not the all-length proof.

For k≥1, keep the first factor 2; each subsequent orientation factor 2 becomes 1+t because exactly one of its two choices makes a switch from the known preceding ending bit. Use t^k for the k fixed internal switches. For the tail this changes R(z) to 1+z(1+t)/(1−z).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The substitution gives exactly 2z^(2k)t^k(1+t)^(k−1)(1+zt)/(1−z)^(k+1). The optional boundaries are independent, so the asserted sharp range follows by counting the available boundaries. This is coefficient extraction from the prior explicit parametrization, not an inference from equality of marginals or merely the abstract existence of a word enumeration.
